# Generated Code Reference

This document is the contract between the generator and your application: what the generated file contains, how the pieces interact, and what each piece costs at runtime. It assumes you've read [DSL.md](DSL.md).

## File header

Every generated file starts with a `Code generated by` marker that matches the convention recognized by `go vet`, `gofmt` (no behavior change), `golangci-lint` (which has its own opt-outs for generated code), and most code-review tools:

```go
// Code generated by github.com/matthewjberger/statemachine; DO NOT EDIT.

package <Package>
```

`<Package>` is the value of the `package:` header in the source `.sm` file.

The file has no `import` statements. All identifiers it produces are either typed integers or strings — nothing requires the standard library at runtime.

## Types

### State enum

```go
type <Prefix>State uint8

const (
    <Prefix>State<NameA> <Prefix>State = iota
    <Prefix>State<NameB>
    <Prefix>State<NameC>
)
```

- The underlying type is `uint8`. This supports up to 256 states. If you need more, the generator will need a one-line change (`uint8` → `uint16`).
- States are declared in the order they first appear in the `.sm` file, scanning source-side first then target-side per transition.
- The zero value of the type is the first declared state. If the user marked a different state with `*`, `Default<Prefix>State()` returns that one — but uninitialized values still come out as the first declared state.

### Event enum

The same pattern, with `Event` instead of `State`. Events are declared in the order they first appear as the right-hand side of a `+`.

## String methods

```go
func (s <Prefix>State) String() string {
    switch s {
    case <Prefix>State<NameA>:
        return "<NameA>"
    ...
    }
    return "Unknown"
}
```

The fallback `"Unknown"` is hit only when a caller constructs an out-of-range value (`<Prefix>State(255)`). For valid values, this is a straight jump-table lookup compiled by Go.

Both `<Prefix>State` and `<Prefix>Event` satisfy `fmt.Stringer`, so `%v` formatting prints the source-file name (`"Idle"`) rather than the integer (`0`).

## All* arrays

```go
var All<Prefix>States = [...]<Prefix>State{<Prefix>State<NameA>, <Prefix>State<NameB>, ...}
var All<Prefix>Events = [...]<Prefix>Event{<Prefix>Event<NameA>, ...}
```

Fixed-size arrays, not slices. `len(All<Prefix>States)` is a constant; the array is laid out in static storage with no allocation. Range-loop them like any slice:

```go
for _, state := range AllLightStates {
    fmt.Println(state, state.ValidEvents())
}
```

If you need a slice, take a slice expression: `AllLightStates[:]`. The slice header points into the static array.

## Default* function

```go
func Default<Prefix>State() <Prefix>State {
    return <Prefix>State<Initial>
}
```

Returns the `*`-marked state, or the first declared state if none is marked. Use this when constructing a fresh state value; it documents intent better than relying on the type's zero value.

## ProcessEvent

```go
func (s <Prefix>State) ProcessEvent(event <Prefix>Event) (<Prefix>State, bool) {
    switch s {
    case <SourceA>:
        switch event {
        case <EventX>:
            return <DestA1>, true
        case <EventY>:
            return <DestA2>, true
        }
    case <SourceB>:
        switch event {
        ...
        }
    }
    switch event {  // wildcard
    case <EventZ>:
        return <Dest>, true
    }
    return s, false
}
```

The contract:

- `(newState, true)` means the transition is valid. Apply it (or guard against it; see below).
- `(s, false)` means the event has no transition from this state. The returned `s` is the receiver unchanged, so a caller that ignores the bool and unconditionally assigns is still safe (no spurious transition).

### Specific-over-wildcard

The outer switch on `s` handles every specific `(state, event)` transition. The second switch on `event` (no outer switch) handles wildcards. Because the specific switch returns first, **a wildcard transition is only reached if the state has no specific entry for that event.** This is the same priority rule as the Rust `stateless` proc-macro.

If you write:

```
*A + Reset = B,
_ + Reset = Z,
```

then `A.ProcessEvent(Reset)` returns `(B, true)`. The wildcard `_ + Reset = Z` applies only to states other than `A`.

### Internal transitions

If a transition's target is `_`, the generated `return` uses the source state:

```
Moving + Tick = _,
```

```go
case StateMoving:
    switch event {
    case EventTick:
        return StateMoving, true   // not "_", which isn't a valid Go const
    }
```

For wildcard internals (`_ + Heartbeat = _`), the generated code returns the receiver:

```go
case EventHeartbeat:
    return s, true
```

In both cases the event is *accepted* (`true`), even though the state doesn't change. This is what lets wrapper code run side effects unconditionally for accepted events:

```go
next, ok := r.state.ProcessEvent(EventTick)
if !ok {
    return
}
r.movementTicks++
r.state = next   // same state, no-op assignment, no need to special-case
```

## ValidEvents

```go
var (
    <prefix>State<NameA>ValidEvents = []<Prefix>Event{<Prefix>Event<EventX>, <Prefix>Event<EventY>}
    <prefix>State<NameB>ValidEvents = []<Prefix>Event{...}
    ...
)

func (s <Prefix>State) ValidEvents() []<Prefix>Event {
    switch s {
    case <Prefix>State<NameA>:
        return <prefix>State<NameA>ValidEvents
    case <Prefix>State<NameB>:
        return <prefix>State<NameB>ValidEvents
    }
    return nil
}
```

- The per-state slice is a **package-scope `var`**, not built inside the method. Calling `ValidEvents()` repeatedly is allocation-free; the returned slice header points at the same backing storage every time.
- The contents are: events that have a specific transition from this state (in declaration order), then wildcard events that apply because the state lacks a specific transition for that event (in declaration order).
- A terminal state (no outgoing transitions and no applicable wildcards) returns an empty but non-nil slice. The `nil` fallback at the end is unreachable for any in-range receiver.

Use this to drive UIs, generate help text, validate input from outside the program, or enumerate valid actions for an AI controller.

The naming convention for the package-scope slice is `lowerFirst(<Prefix>State) + <Name> + "ValidEvents"`, e.g. `lightStateRedValidEvents`. This is unexported by convention but is technically usable from other files in the same package if you need to introspect it.

## DOT graph

```go
const <Prefix>DOT = `digraph {
  rankdir=LR;
  node [shape=circle];
  "<Initial>" [shape=doublecircle];
  "<Src>" -> "<Dst>" [label="<Event>"];
  ...
}`
```

- A `const` `string`, not a `var`. Go's linker drops unused `const` strings from the final binary; if you never reference `<Prefix>DOT`, it costs zero bytes.
- The initial state is rendered as a `doublecircle`.
- Specific transitions appear first, in source-file order.
- Wildcard transitions are expanded: one edge per `(state, event)` combination where the state has no specific transition for that event.

Pipe the value through Graphviz to render it:

```bash
go run ./your-tool | dot -Tpng -o states.png
```

Where `./your-tool` is anything that does `fmt.Println(<Prefix>DOT)`.

## Cost model

| Construct           | Runtime cost                                  | Binary cost                       |
|---------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Enum constants      | Zero (compile-time integers)                  | One byte per value                |
| `String()`          | One switch (jump table)                       | Method body + name strings        |
| `All*` arrays       | Zero (static)                                 | `len(states) * 1` bytes           |
| `Default*()`        | One return                                    | Method body                       |
| `ProcessEvent`      | Two nested switches, no allocations           | Method body                       |
| `ValidEvents`       | One switch + slice header return, no allocations | Per-state backing array (1 byte per event in the slice) |
| `DOT` const         | Zero (compile-time string)                    | Length of the DOT text, **only if referenced** |

The generated file does no runtime registration, no map lookups, no reflection. Once compiled, the only state machine cost is the integer switch in `ProcessEvent`.
